section_summary: This section contains U.S. State Department records from March to August 1939 regarding Japanese internal political affairs, foreign relations, and military activities in China. It comprises concluding lists of despatches and telegrams for the Tokyo Embassy's March 1939 monthly report, complete text and transmittal for the April 1939 monthly report (Report No. 151), the initial portion of the May 1939 monthly report (Report No. 152), and evaluative memoranda by the Division of Far Eastern Affairs. Key topics include Japanese-American relations surrounding the USS Astoria's ceremonial mission returning former Ambassador Saito's ashes, tensions over North China trade controls and aerial bombings of American mission property, Japanese pressure on foreign concessions at Shanghai and Kulangsu, the annexation of the Spratly Islands, the Soviet-Japanese fisheries agreement, and domestic war-mobilization policies under the National Mobilization Law.

subfiles.about: Concluding appendices of the Tokyo Embassy's March 1939 monthly report, listing despatches and telegrams sent to the Department of State.
subfiles.summary: This document represents the concluding pages of Embassy Tokyo's Report No. 150 on conditions in Japan for March 1939. It contains a chronological list of despatches Nos. 3759 through 3793 sent between March 16 and March 31, 1939, detailing subjects such as the Anti-Comintern Pact, Sino-Japanese hostilities, naval estimates, and bombings of American mission property. It also includes a register of telegrams Nos. 115 through 161 dispatched to the State Department during March 1939, addressing the return of former Ambassador Saito's ashes, trade restrictions in North China, European developments, and the Japanese occupation of the Spratly Islands.
subfiles.title: Embassy Tokyo Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of March, 1939 (Despatches and Telegrams Lists)

subfiles.about: Internal memorandum evaluating Tokyo Embassy's April 1939 monthly political report and recommending substantial reduction in its length.
subfiles.summary: Memo criticizes Tokyo's bloated April 1939 report for redundant summaries, recommending shorter future reports and dropping the unreliable China military-operations section.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Tokyo's Monthly Report for April 1939

subfiles.about: Tokyo Embassy monthly political report (No. 151) transmitting comprehensive coverage of conditions in Japan during April 1939.
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman, Chargé d'Affaires a.i., American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 3912 transmits Tokyo Embassy Report No. 151 reviewing political, diplomatic, and economic developments in Japan during April 1939. Relations with the United States were highlighted by the ceremonial arrival of the USS Astoria bearing the ashes of the late Ambassador Hiroshi Saito, alongside diplomatic representations regarding North China trade restrictions, narcotics traffic, and bombings of American mission property. In foreign relations, the report details military operations in China (including the Chinese 'April offensive'), Japanese annexation of the Spratly Islands over British and French protests, conclusion of a Soviet-Japanese fisheries modus vivendi, and Cabinet discussions on the Anti-Comintern Pact. Domestic developments include the appointments of General Koiso as Overseas Minister and Mr. Tanabe as Communications Minister, factional split in the Seiyukai party, invocation of Articles 6 and 11 of the National Mobilization Law, and adoption of a national commodity price control plan.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 3912: Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of April, 1939 (Report No. 151)

subfiles.about: Brief memorandum assessing the Tokyo Embassy's May 1939 monthly report and highlighting Japanese press assertions on aerial bombings.
subfiles.from: Laurence E. Salisbury, Division of Far Eastern Affairs
subfiles.summary: Memo finds May 1939's report unremarkable, noting inaccurate Japanese press denials that Chungking was undefended and claims bombing targeted only military sites.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Tokyo's Monthly Report for May 1939

subfiles.about: Tokyo Embassy monthly political report (No. 152) detailing conditions in Japan and diplomatic relations during May 1939.
subfiles.from: Eugene H. Dooman, Chargé d'Affaires a.i., American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 3999 transmits Report No. 152 covering conditions in Japan for May 1939 (pages 181 to 195 cover the report through the beginning of Ambassador Grew's departure). Relations with the United States centered on Japanese demands to revise the administration and Land Regulations of the International Settlement at Shanghai, the Japanese marine landing at Kulangsu (Amoy), and urgent American protests against indiscriminate aerial bombardments of civilian populations in Chungking and other cities. The report also addresses repeated bombings of American missionary properties, commercial restrictions placed on the Universal Leaf Tobacco Company in Shantung, travel restrictions on Americans at Hankow, and Ambassador Grew's departure for home leave on May 19.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 3999: Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of May, 1939 (Report No. 152)
